role: Block.onBlockActivated for every activatable 1.7.10 block (doors, trapdoor, fence gate, buttons, lever, bed with the sleep checks, cake, note block, jukebox with disc insert/eject, repeater, comparator, flower pot, cauldron, chests including trapped/ender and the double-chest pairing, furnace, dispenser, workbench, dragon egg teleport), the front half of ItemInWorldManager.activateBlockOrUseItem. Runs both as the ActivateProbe case machine (act_init/act_case_begin/act_run/act_case_end) and as the live right-click path survival.c calls (act_live_block, act_live_chest_close, act_live_dragon_egg).

structs.name: act_env
structs.java: the probe's player, world Random, block events, open container and spawned items for one ActivateProbe case

structs.name: act_live_env
structs.java: the live C08 block-placement packet's server context: world Random, Det streams, item entity list, food and held stack, the player's inventory

structs.name: ids
structs.java: block/item/material ids resolved by registry name once

gpu: its former globals, function statics and lazily built tables are gone (lane/gpuenv, L2): per-environment state lives in struct env (csrc/engine/env.h), per-dimension state in the replay's dims, constant tables are built before main; csrc/tests/globals.sh lists what is left
line 49-65, functions block_named and item_named: linear string searches of the registries, exit(2) on a missing name
lines 980-997, function act_live_block: saves, overwrites and restores the global blockcb_env (blockcb.c) around the call
line 326, function act_item_drop, and line 1066, function act_live_env_drop: calloc of an ie_ent per dropped item inside the tick
line 261, function act_spawn_item: ie_spawn_item allocates item entities in item_entity.c (not verified in that file)
line 221-235, function inv_player_add: do/while over the slots until the stack stops shrinking; bounded by the 36 slots in practice
act_env carries function pointers (on_write, saved_write) and a struct world pointer
notes: Sleep itself is recorded (branch order and refusals), not simulated; what a sleeping player does is sleep.c. Redstone is switched off (world.conf), so button, lever, repeater and comparator activations only flip meta and schedule ticks; the comparator's input strength is taken as 0. The jukebox disc insert (ItemRecord.onItemUse) is the only reachable item half. Container GUIs are a gui flag here; the container contents are container.c. The redstone ore ids are resolved but their activation path was not read in detail. Member names for block classes are MCP names from comments, not diffed against each Java file.
